analysis.title: Why Is Everyone Hiding When PMIs Are Strong? Goldman Maps The Quiet Defensive Rotation Across Every Asset Class
key_insights: Goldman's cross-asset sentiment and positioning indicator fell to the 46th percentile, its lowest since April, decoupled from continued strong Global PMIs. Larger fixed income fund flows, a drop below zero in the Risk Appetite Indicator, and more positioning in gold and JPY were the largest drags.
The indicator averages percentile ranks across 16 sentiment and positioning measures and has broadly tracked the Global Composite PMI since 2007. PMIs are holding up while positioning rolls over.

Safe bond flows (3m and 12m), CTA equity beta and JPY and gold futures positioning sit in the bottom fifth of their ranges. US equity CFTC positioning and global equity fund flows are still above roughly the 90th percentile (approximate, read off the chart).

In the GOAL Kickstart note 'AI concerns weigh further on risk appetite', Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator turned negative for the first time since March 2026, with all five sub-components down over the past month. Credit and equity vol led the decline.

Equity vol rose modestly last week, much less than bond vol, while systematic investors (CTAs, risk parity) remain risk-off. Hedge fund net leverage fell sharply in recent days while gross leverage stayed broadly unchanged. Net leverage is at its lowest since spring and gross is near the top of its two-year range.

AAII survey: conviction is high and above the year-to-date median, with an roughly even split between bulls and bears. Per Goldman, when AAII readings are neutral but conviction is high, subsequent S&P 500 returns are more volatile, about 22% annualized over three months versus about 10.5% after low-conviction readings (approximate, from the chart).

Bonds are the clearest destination for fund flows. Bond fund flows have outpaced equity flows in US and Western European funds, led by short-term government and inflation-protected funds. US short-term government funds took in roughly 29% of AuM year to date versus about 3% for US equity funds, and Western European equity funds are slightly negative (approximate).
CLO ETFs kept attracting inflows as a high-carry alternative in securitized credit. 30-day rolling flows into the 29 tracked funds ($57.6B AuM) are back above $5B, near the early-2025 high.

Rates positioning remains bearish but less so in the front end. Asset manager net DV01 in bond and ultra-bond futures fell from about $24B per 100bp to about $14B in a matter of weeks (approximate). Goldman's Fund Positioning Indicator shows a shift to underweight duration during the recent selloff.

Per Bloomberg, CME open interest fell again across 5-year, 10-year, ultra 10-year and long-bond futures, a combined $8.4 million per DV01. Long-bond open interest is down about $12 million per DV01 since Oct 7 and fell in six of the last seven sessions.

European money market funds saw some of the strongest flow swings in recent years as sovereign risk repricing hit excess liquidity and reserves. Flatter yield curves have historically preceded stronger money market inflows.
Momentum ETFs lost an estimated $5.1B in September, among the largest monthly outflows in recent years, out of $88B in AuM. The next-largest outflow since January 2023 was about $1.6B.

Global leveraged Tech ETF AuM fell from a June 22 peak of roughly $135B. Korea and Taiwan products fell from about $70B to the low $30s (approximate). The week of Oct 12-16 still saw the largest weekly inflow into levered ETFs on Goldman's record, including a record $7B into SOXL, so AuM is falling because of prices, not because dip buyers left.

Sector flows over four weeks: Telecoms had the strongest flows relative to AuM, with Utilities and Infrastructure also gaining. Financials and Industrials had the largest outflows and Consumer Goods was also negative. Technology and Energy took in money last week.

Speculators increased long JPY exposure and cut net short CHF futures, despite stronger USD positioning. Non-commercial JPY positioning swung over a matter of weeks and CHF shorts were trimmed to about -$3B (approximate). EUR and GBP positioning remains very negative.

Gold futures positioning remains elevated and physical ETF holdings have risen despite recent price weakness. The price contribution to ETF reserves since January 2025 fell from a peak near $250B to about $135B, while the quantity contribution reached a new high above $60B (approximate).

Goldman shifted to overweight equities on a three-month view, alongside overweight cash, while staying underweight credit and neutral duration. It cites earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations into year-end, with near-term volatility risk from AI concerns, Middle East tensions and midterm elections.
Goldman's Kickstart note pitches VIX call spreads as a cheap tactical hedge because dispersion keeps the VIX low relative to credit.

Author's view (ZeroHedge, not Goldman): positioning is not yet light. A 46th percentile reading is mid-range, and hedge fund gross leverage, US equity futures and global equity fund flows remain near the top of their ranges. A true contrarian low usually follows falling gross and negative equity flows, neither of which has happened.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees lighter positioning, lower valuations and earnings support lifting equities into year-end, so it is overweight equities on a three-month view.
tension_points.bear_case: The author says a 46th percentile reading is mid-range, hedge fund gross leverage, US equity futures and global equity fund flows are near the top of their ranges, and the long book has not been cleaned out.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A true contrarian low usually comes after gross leverage falls and equity flows turn negative, and neither has happened.

theme_stances.key_argument: Investors are buying bonds, gold, yen and puts while macro data stays strong, but the long equity book has not been cleaned out.
theme_stances.evidence: Positioning is defensive everywhere except where it counts.
